title: Understanding SVD
text: The singular value decomposition (SVD) of a matrix X is given by X=U*S*V**T. Here, U and V are orthogonal matrices, and S is a diagonal matrix containing the singular values.

title: Properties of U
text: The columns of U are the left singular vectors of X. They are not necessarily the eigenvectors of $$X^T X$$, but they are related to the eigenvectors of $$X X^T$$.

title: True or False?
text: Are the columns of matrix U always the eigenvectors of $$X^T X$$?
